Keywords: Winter seed fuel and care burdens
RagShortTexts: Seed, meals and dues compete for household stores.
Care of the sick needs fuel, labor and shelter.

Variants.Content: Winter survival combines grain, preserved food, fuel and shelter. Stores must cover seed and dues as well as meals. Sick people need attendants, warm food and protection from cold; mead is a drink, not a substitute for care.
An injured soldier needs attendants and carrying, not simply another ration entry. Wet clothing and cold complicate recovery; nursing reduces guard strength.
Leaving seed and food for vulnerable people protects another harvest. Assigning casualties to already depleted households deepens shortages despite full collection accounts.
Illness removes labor while adding fuel and care work. Borrowing, eating less or selling tools carries costs; neighbors’ help can determine winter survival.
